message.content:
Let the volume be \(V\). For vectors \(\mathbf a,\mathbf b,\mathbf c\), the volume of the parallelepiped is

\[
V=\left|\det(\mathbf a,\mathbf b,\mathbf c)\right|.
\]

Equivalently,

\[
V^2=\det(G),
\]

where \(G\) is the Gram matrix of dot products.

Since each vector has norm \(2\),

\[
\mathbf a\cdot \mathbf a=\mathbf b\cdot \mathbf b=\mathbf c\cdot \mathbf c=4.
\]

Also, the angle between any two vectors satisfies

\[
\cos\theta=\frac58,
\]

so for any distinct pair,

\[
\mathbf a\cdot \mathbf b=\mathbf a\cdot \mathbf c=\mathbf b\cdot \mathbf c
=2\cdot 2\cdot \frac58
=\frac52.
\]

Thus

\[
G=
\begin{pmatrix}
4 & \frac52 & \frac52\\
\frac52 & 4 & \frac52\\
\frac52 & \frac52 & 4
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

This matrix has diagonal entries \(4\) and off-diagonal entries \(\frac52\). Its eigenvalues are

\[
4+2\cdot \frac52=9
\]

and

\[
4-\frac52=\frac32
\]

with multiplicity \(2\). Therefore,

\[
\det(G)=9\left(\frac32\right)^2
=9\cdot \frac94
=\frac{81}{4}.
\]

Hence

\[
V^2=\frac{81}{4},
\]

so

\[
V=\frac92.
\]

The answer is \(\boxed{\frac92}\).
